GAAP diluted EPS is guided to $0.68 to $0.76 and non-GAAP diluted EPS to $0.84 to $0.92. The product revenue range sits above the $114.3 million reported for the third quarter, while royalties are guided below the $77.0 million just posted.
items.source_name: Rambus press release via Business Wire (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: FirstSun Q3 net income $38.4M, $0.82 per share, vs Q2 net loss of $22.9M; NIM 3.82%
items.take: FirstSun Capital Bancorp reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $38.4 million, or $0.82 per diluted share, versus a net loss of $22.9 million in the prior quarter and net income of $23.2 million a year earlier. Net interest margin increased 24 basis points from the prior quarter to 3.82%, loans fell to $11.5 billion from $11.6 billion at June 30, and deposits were $13.0 billion versus $13.4 billion. The common equity tier 1 ratio was 11.99%; diluted EPS was $0.82 in both the third quarter of 2026 and 2025 even as net income rose.
items.source_name: FirstSun Capital Bancorp press release via Business Wire (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: HBT Financial Q3 diluted EPS $0.86 vs $0.63; net income $31.4M
items.take: HBT Financial reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $31.4 million, or $0.86 per diluted share, versus $19.8 million and $0.63 in the third quarter of 2025 and $27.8 million and $0.76 in the second quarter of 2026. Net income is up about 58.6% year over year on our calculation. The loan book was far larger than a year ago ($4.78 billion versus $3.40 billion), so much of the earnings gain came with a bigger balance sheet.
items.source_name: HBT Financial press release via GlobeNewswire (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: HBT Financial net interest margin 4.35% vs 4.13%; loans $4.78B, deposits $5.75B
items.take: HBT Financial reported a third-quarter 2026 net interest margin of 4.35%, compared with 4.32% in Q2 2026 and 4.13% in Q3 2025. Total loans were $4.78 billion at Sept. 30, 2026 versus $4.75 billion at June 30 and $3.40 billion a year earlier; deposits were $5.75 billion versus $5.76 billion at June 30 and $4.35 billion a year earlier. Quarter-on-quarter balance sheet growth was small, so the year-over-year step-up is the story.
items.source_name: HBT Financial press release via GlobeNewswire (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Freddie Mac launches cash tender for five STACR note classes; expires Oct. 30
items.take: Freddie Mac announced a fixed-price cash tender offer for five STACR classes: 2020-HQA5 B-1, 2021-DNA3 B-1, 2021-DNA5 B-1, 2021-HQA1 B-1 and 2023-DNA2 M-1B. Offer prices range from $1,035.17 to $1,135.00 per $1,000 original principal, plus accrued interest. The offer expires at 5 p.m. New York time on Oct. 30, 2026 unless extended, with settlement expected Nov. 3. The five classes total $1.125 billion of original principal on our calculation; the release does not state an aggregate.
items.source_name: Freddie Mac press release via GlobeNewswire (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Fed calendar: FOMC meets Oct. 27-28; press conference listed for 2:30 p.m. ET Oct. 28
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's October calendar lists a two-day FOMC meeting on Oct. 27-28, with a press conference listed at 2:30 p.m. ET on Oct. 28. The calendar also shows the H.4.1 reserve balances release at 4:30 p.m. ET on Oct. 29 and the H.8 commercial bank balance sheet release at 4:15 p.m. ET on Oct. 30. Those releases land right after the meeting, giving a first official read on Fed balance sheet and bank data once the decision is out.

items.headline: Dallas Fed Texas factory output index 15.8 in October vs 29.5 in September
items.take: The Dallas Fed's Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey, released Oct. 26, put the production index at 15.8 in October versus 29.5 in September, and the new orders index at 9.3 versus 30.7. The Dallas Fed headlined the report "Texas manufacturing activity remains solid, though pace of growth moderates." Both readings fell by double digits, while the general business activity index rose to 13.4 from 9.8.
items.source_name: Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Dallas Fed: Texas raw-material prices-paid index 55.3 in October vs 52.2
items.take: In the Dallas Fed's October Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey, the raw materials prices paid index was 55.3, up from 52.2 in September, while the employment index was 11.6 versus 15.1. The general business activity index was 13.4 versus 9.8. Higher input-price readings alongside slower hiring and orders growth is a mix worth watching ahead of this week's FOMC meeting.
items.source_name: Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: First Resource Bancorp Q3 diluted EPS $0.98 vs $0.75; net income $2.94M
items.take: First Resource Bancorp reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $2,940,474 versus $2,258,166 a year earlier, and diluted EPS of $0.98 versus $0.75. Net interest margin was 4.06% versus 3.87%. Total assets were $887.6 million and deposits $789.6 million at Sept. 30, so earnings growth came alongside a larger balance sheet.
items.source_name: First Resource Bancorp press release via PR Newswire (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Verizon Q3 revenue $34.3B, up 1.5%; diluted EPS $1.25 vs $1.17
items.take: Verizon reported third-quarter 2026 operating revenue of $34,313 million versus $33,821 million a year earlier, and diluted EPS of $1.25 versus $1.17. Net income attributable to Verizon was $5,198 million versus $4,950 million. Revenue growth was modest against faster EPS growth, which points to profit rising more than sales this quarter.

items.headline: Verizon raises 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $5.04-$5.06; Q3 postpaid phone adds 406,000
items.take: Verizon raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $5.04 to $5.06, or 7.0 to 7.5 percent growth, up from 6.0 to 7.0 percent, and postpaid phone net additions to 1.1 million to 1.2 million. Third-quarter postpaid phone net additions were 406,000 versus 44,000 a year earlier, and free cash flow was $7.8 billion, up 12.1 percent. The subscriber swing is the main driver behind the higher outlook.

items.headline: Bank of Hawaii Q3 diluted EPS $1.49 vs $1.20; net income $64.3M
items.take: Bank of Hawaii reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $64.3 million, or $1.49 per diluted share, versus $53.3 million and $1.20 in the third quarter of 2025. The board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.70 per share, the same as a year earlier. The year-over-year gain in earnings coincided with a wider margin and a lower efficiency ratio.

items.headline: Bank of Hawaii net interest margin 2.82% vs 2.46%; CET1 ratio 12.10%
items.take: Bank of Hawaii's net interest margin was 2.82% in the third quarter of 2026 versus 2.46% a year earlier, and its CET1 ratio was 12.10% at Sept. 30 versus 11.98% a year before (preliminary). Total loans and leases were $14.4 billion, up 2.1% from Dec. 31, 2025, while total deposits were $20.5 billion, down 3.3% over the same span. Loans growing while deposits shrink is a funding mix worth watching for regional banks.

items.headline: Easterly Government Properties Q3 FFO $0.79/share vs $0.74; raises low end of 2026 guide
items.take: Easterly Government Properties reported third-quarter 2026 total revenues of $93.6 million versus $86.2 million and fully diluted FFO per share of $0.79 versus $0.74. Core FFO per share was $0.78 versus $0.76, and the company raised the lower end of its 2026 Core FFO range to $3.08-$3.13 while introducing a 2027 range of $3.09-$3.17. The narrow guidance bands signal steady, lease-driven cash flow.

items.headline: Medifast Q3 revenue $72.0M, down 19.4%; net loss $17.5M, or $1.57 per share
items.take: Medifast reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $72.0 million, down 19.4% from $89.4 million, and a net loss of $17.5 million, or $1.57 per share, versus a loss of $2.3 million, or $0.21 per share. Independent active earning coaches were 10,200 versus 19,500 a year earlier, and it guides fourth-quarter revenue of $55-$75 million. The halving of the coach base is the key driver behind the sales decline.

items.headline: Umios to acquire High Liner Foods for C$27.00 per share in cash, about C$804M
items.take: Umios Corporation agreed to acquire High Liner Foods for C$27.00 per share in cash, valuing the equity at approximately C$804 million, in a court-approved plan of arrangement. Completion is expected in January 2027, subject to approval by 75% of votes cast by High Liner shareholders, Competition Act (Canada) approval and U.S. Hart-Scott-Rodino clearance. Shareholders holding about 45.4% of shares have signed voting support agreements, which lowers the shareholder-vote hurdle.

items.headline: Umios to fund High Liner purchase mainly with interest-bearing debt and cash on hand
items.take: Umios said it will fund the C$804 million equity purchase of High Liner Foods mainly with interest-bearing debt and cash on hand. The release does not disclose an enterprise value or premium. The financing structure means the deal adds to Umios' borrowings rather than being paid in stock.

items.headline: Endeavor Bancorp Q3 diluted EPS $0.44 vs $0.36 a year ago; net income $2.12M
items.take: Endeavor Bancorp reported Q3 2026 net income of $2.12 million, or $0.44 per diluted share, versus $1.89 million ($0.40) in Q2 2026 and $1.73 million ($0.36) in Q3 2025. Net interest margin was 4.41%, unchanged from Q2 and up from 4.09% a year earlier. Per-share earnings rose 22% year over year.

items.headline: Endeavor Bancorp loans $644.9M, down from $664.8M in Q2; deposits $731.2M
items.take: Endeavor reported total loans of $644.9 million at Sept. 30, down from $664.8 million at June 30 and up from $632.6 million a year earlier. Total deposits were $731.2 million versus $725.0 million at June 30 and $678.3 million a year earlier. Tangible book value per share rose to $15.46 from $15.11 at June 30.

items.headline: Business First Q3 diluted EPS $0.71 vs $0.73 a year ago; net income $23.2M
items.take: Business First Bancshares reported Q3 net income available to common shareholders of $23.2 million, or $0.71 per diluted share, versus $0.70 in Q2 2026 and $0.73 in Q3 2025. The board declared a common dividend of $0.15 per share, payable Nov. 30 to holders of record Nov. 15. Per-share earnings slipped slightly from a year ago even as net income rose from $21.5 million.

items.headline: Business First net interest margin widens 13 bp to 3.86%; loans up $121.4M in Q3
items.take: Business First said its net interest margin expanded 13 basis points to 3.86% from 3.73% in Q2 2026 and 3.68% a year earlier. Loans held for investment rose $121.4 million, or 1.82%, to $6,780.9 million, while deposits increased $141.2 million, or 1.95%, to $7,376.8 million. Deposit growth outpacing loan growth in dollars gives the bank room on funding.

items.headline: KeyCorp Q3 diluted EPS $0.51 vs $0.41; revenue $2.04B, up 8%
items.take: KeyCorp reported Q3 net income from continuing operations attributable to common shareholders of $537 million, versus $454 million a year earlier, with diluted EPS of $0.51 versus $0.41. The company cited record revenue of $2.04 billion, up 8% year over year and 4% sequentially. Taxable-equivalent net interest margin was 2.95%, up 20 basis points from a year ago.

items.headline: KeyCorp estimated CET1 ratio 11.1% at Sept. 30; average loans $111.6B
items.take: KeyCorp reported an estimated CET1 ratio of 11.1% at Sept. 30, 2026. Average loans held for investment were $111.6 billion, up $5.4 billion from Q3 2025, and average deposits were $151.2 billion, up $801 million. The company declared a dividend of $0.205 per common share during the quarter.

items.headline: Live Oak Q3 diluted EPS $0.52 vs $0.55; net interest margin 3.30%
items.take: Live Oak Bancshares reported Q3 net income attributable to common shareholders of $24.3 million, or $0.52 per diluted share, versus $25.6 million and $0.55 a year earlier. Total loans and leases were $13.87 billion versus $11.92 billion, and total deposits were $15.47 billion versus $13.29 billion. Net interest margin was 3.30% versus 3.33%.

items.headline: Third Coast Bancshares to acquire Great Plains Bancshares in all-stock deal valued at ~$239.6M
items.take: Third Coast Bancshares and Great Plains Bancshares announced a definitive merger agreement in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $239.6 million based on Third Coast's Oct. 6 closing price; Third Coast expects to issue 5,570,352 shares. Closing is expected in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and approval by both companies' shareholders. The companies said combined total assets would exceed $9 billion.

items.headline: Acuity reaches definitive agreement to acquire Parameter Technologies for $675M
items.take: Acuity said it has reached a definitive agreement to acquire Parameter Technologies, a Fort Collins, Colorado maker of monitoring and detection solutions for data centers, utilities and critical infrastructure, for a $675 million purchase price. Closing is expected in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, subject to customary conditions including expiration of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period. Parameter would join Distech Controls within Acuity Intelligent Spaces.

items.headline: Acuity to fund $675M Parameter deal with $500M of borrowings plus cash on hand
items.take: Acuity said the $675 million purchase price will be paid with $500 million in borrowings, with the remainder from balance sheet cash; J.P. Morgan and Bank of America are leading the financing. Acuity stated Parameter expects sales of approximately $100 million for calendar 2027 with growth above 30 percent and EBITDA margins of approximately 40 percent. These are the company's projections, not reported results, and they show the deal is being priced on forward expectations.

items.headline: Lakeland Financial Q3 diluted EPS $1.14 vs $1.03; net income $28.9M
items.take: Lakeland Financial reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $28.9 million versus $26.4 million in Q3 2025, and diluted EPS of $1.14 versus $1.03, up 11% as the company states. Net interest margin was 3.58% versus 3.50% a year earlier. Margin expansion alongside loan growth is the combination that drives bank earnings per share.
items.source_name: Lakeland Financial Corp. Q3 2026 results release (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Lakeland loans up $431.4M, or 8%, year over year to $5.68B; CET1 14.46%
items.take: Lakeland said total loans rose $431.4 million, or 8%, from $5.25 billion to $5.68 billion between Sept. 30, 2025 and Sept. 30, 2026. Total assets were about $7.21 billion, with a total capital ratio of 15.56%, CET1 of 14.46% and Tier 1 leverage of 12.36%, which the company noted are preliminary until the FR Y-9C is filed. Capital ratios at that level leave room to keep lending.
items.source_name: Lakeland Financial Corp. Q3 2026 results release (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Citizens Community Bancorp Q3 EPS $0.56 vs $0.37; dividend raised 14% to $0.12
items.take: Citizens Community Bancorp reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $5.4 million and diluted EPS of $0.56 versus $0.37 a year earlier. Net interest margin was 3.37%, up from 3.22% in the second quarter. The board raised the quarterly dividend 14% to $0.12 per share from $0.105, payable Nov. 20 to holders of record Nov. 6.
items.source_name: Citizens Community Bancorp Q3 2026 results release (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Treasury tentative schedule: 2-year note today, 5-year Oct. 27, 7-year Oct. 29
items.take: Treasury's tentative auction schedule lists a 2-year note auction today, a 5-year note on Tuesday Oct. 27, a 2-year FRN on Wednesday Oct. 28 and a 7-year note on Thursday Oct. 29, with the three notes and the FRN settling Nov. 2. Weekly bill auctions run alongside, including 13- and 26-week bills today. The schedule is marked tentative, so sizes come only with the official announcements.

items.headline: EQT to acquire Range Resources in all-stock deal; 0.987 EQT shares per Range share
items.take: EQT said each Range common share will be exchanged for 0.987 EQT shares, leaving EQT holders with about 73% and Range holders about 27% of the combined company, which it put at a pro forma enterprise value over $50 billion. EQT expects $325 million of base annual synergies within two years, with a pathway to more than $600 million long term, and closing in the first quarter of 2027. The release states no dollar purchase price, so the $50 billion figure describes combined size, not deal value.
items.source_name: EQT Corp. Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1 press release (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Ovintiv to acquire Logan Energy at C$1.40 per share in cash; about US$890M
items.take: Ovintiv agreed to buy Logan Energy for C$1.40 per share in cash, a total value of about C$1.26 billion (about US$890 million) that includes Logan's expected net debt at closing. The release describes about 266,000 net acres in the Montney oil window and Logan production of about 20 MBOE/d, and says Logan will spin out Logan Oil Corp. to its shareholders; closing is expected early in the first quarter of 2027. No premium is stated, and because the value includes net debt it is not an equity-only figure.
items.source_name: Ovintiv Inc. Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1 press release (Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Corxel US, Amanat Acquisition Corp agree to combine; about $377M proceeds expected
items.take: Amanat Acquisition Corp (Nasdaq: AMAN) and Corxel US, an obesity-focused biopharma, signed a definitive business combination agreement, with the combined company expected to list on the Nasdaq Capital Market under a name and ticker still to be announced. The release cites about $75 million in Amanat's trust account and an expected PIPE of about $300 million, for approximately $377 million of total expected gross proceeds assuming no redemptions; closing is expected in the first half of 2027. No pro forma valuation is disclosed, so deal size cannot be compared with other biotech listings yet.
items.source_name: Corxel US and Amanat Acquisition Corp release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: HBT Financial Q3 net income $31.4M, or $0.86 per diluted share, vs $19.8M and $0.63
items.take: HBT Financial reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $31.4 million, or $0.86 per diluted share, versus $19.8 million, or $0.63, a year earlier and $27.8 million, or $0.76, in the second quarter. By our calculation net income rose 58.8% and diluted EPS rose 36.5% year over year. Return on average assets was 1.85% and the efficiency ratio 48.73%.
items.source_name: HBT Financial Q3 2026 results release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: HBT net interest margin 4.35% vs 4.13% a year ago; CET1 ratio 12.94%
items.take: HBT Financial's net interest margin was 4.35% in Q3 2026 versus 4.13% a year earlier and 4.32% in Q2. Total assets were $6.7 billion, loans $4.78 billion and deposits $5.75 billion at Sept. 30, with nonperforming assets at 0.16% of total assets and a common equity tier 1 ratio of 12.94%. Tri-County Financial Group's stockholder vote on HBT's pending acquisition of it is scheduled for Oct. 29, with closing expected early in Q1 2027, subject to approvals.
items.source_name: HBT Financial Q3 2026 results release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 26, 2026)

items.headline: Amkor to report Q3 results after Nasdaq close today; call at 5 p.m. ET
items.take: Amkor Technology said it will issue third-quarter 2026 results after the close of trading on Monday, Oct. 26, with a conference call and webcast at 5 p.m. ET. The company's announcement was issued Oct. 5. Figures will be added to the Wire once the release is out.
items.source_name: Amkor Technology announcement of Q3 2026 results date (Nasdaq, Oct. 5, 2026)

items.headline: Rogers Q3 revenue C$5,443M, up 2%; adjusted EBITDA C$2,535M, up 1%
items.take: Rogers reported Q3 2026 total revenue of C$5,443M versus C$5,348M a year earlier, adjusted EBITDA of C$2,535M versus C$2,515M, and free cash flow of C$1,370M versus C$829M. Net income was C$495M versus C$5,768M, with the comparison reflecting a $5 billion non-cash gain on its MLSE stake in Q3 2025. The cash-flow rebound outpaced a flat EBITDA line, which is the part of the quarter worth watching.
items.source_name: Rogers Communications Q3 2026 results release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: Rogers Q3 diluted EPS C$0.88 vs C$10.54; adjusted C$1.29 vs C$1.37
items.take: Rogers' Q3 diluted EPS attributable to shareholders was C$0.88 versus C$10.54 a year earlier; adjusted diluted EPS was C$1.29 versus C$1.37. The company declared a C$0.50 per share dividend on Oct. 22 and reaffirmed its 2026 outlook. Adjusted EPS slipped while the reported swing was driven by last year's one-time gain.
items.source_name: Rogers Communications Q3 2026 results release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: Enova Q3 revenue $1,009.2M, up 26%; diluted EPS $4.06 vs $3.03
items.take: Enova reported Q3 2026 total revenue of $1,009,172K versus $802,678K a year earlier, net income of $107,304K versus $80,314K, and adjusted EPS of $4.48 versus $3.36. The company repurchased $46 million of stock in the quarter and began Q4 with $252 million of repurchase capacity. Revenue and EPS grew at a similar pace, which points to growth driven by balance-sheet expansion rather than margin.
items.source_name: Enova Q3 2026 results release (PR Newswire, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Enova combined receivables $5.90B, up 30%; Q3 originations $2.57B, up 31%
items.take: Enova's combined loan and finance receivable balance, including accrued fees and interest, was $5,897,876K at Sept. 30, 2026 versus $4,521,110K a year earlier. Q3 originations and purchases were $2,567,480K versus $1,961,439K. Receivables and originations both grew about 30%, so the loan book is expanding broadly in line with revenue.
items.source_name: Enova Q3 2026 results release (PR Newswire, Oct. 22, 2026)

items.headline: Rithm Q3 GAAP EPS $0.38; earnings available for distribution $0.55 per share
items.take: Rithm Capital reported Q3 2026 GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders of $217.1M, or $0.38 per diluted share, versus $20.2M, or $0.04, in Q2. Earnings available for distribution were $315.3M, or $0.55 per diluted share, versus $0.60 in Q2, and book value per common share was $12.51. GAAP earnings rose sharply from Q2 while distributable earnings eased, and the $0.25 common dividend stayed unchanged.
items.source_name: Rithm Capital Q3 2026 results release (Business Wire, Oct. 23, 2026)

items.headline: BoJ accounts: JGB holdings ¥504.0T on Oct. 20, up ¥368.7B from Oct. 10
items.take: The Bank of Japan's accounts for Oct. 20 show JGBs held of ¥504.0T versus ¥503.6T on Oct. 10, a rise of ¥368.7B. Total assets were ¥625.0T, up ¥345.3B, while current deposits rose ¥10.19T to ¥418.3T. The balance sheet is still expanding at the margin even as the BoJ heads into its Oct. 29-30 policy meeting.

items.headline: NAR schedule: October existing-home sales Nov. 12; pending sales Nov. 18
items.take: NAR's 2026 statistical release schedule lists October Existing-Home Sales for Thursday, Nov. 12, and the October Pending Home Sales Index for Wednesday, Nov. 18. NAR says all releases are distributed at 10 a.m. Eastern. The November reports follow on Dec. 9 and Dec. 17, giving the housing calendar two prints each month.

items.headline: EIA: weekly petroleum report follows standard Wednesday schedule, Oct. 28 at 10:30 a.m.
items.take: EIA's Weekly Petroleum Status Report schedule lists no exception for the week of Oct. 26-Nov. 1, so the standard release time of 10:30 a.m. Eastern on Wednesday applies. That puts the next crude and product inventory data on Oct. 28, the same day as the Fed decision window the FOMC calendar sets.

items.headline: Census: September trade report due Nov. 4; October report Dec. 8, both 8:30 a.m. ET
items.take: The Census Bureau's foreign trade schedule lists the U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services report for Wednesday, Nov. 4, covering September, and Tuesday, Dec. 8, covering October. Census states all releases occur at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. The September report is the next full trade-balance reading after the third-quarter GDP advance estimate.

items.headline: RBNZ OCR at 2.75% after Sept. 2 hike; next review Oct. 28 at 2 p.m. NZT
items.take: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand raised the Official Cash Rate 25 basis points to 2.75% on Sept. 2, with the MPC saying inflation rose to 4.1% in the June quarter because of higher fuel prices. The Bank's calendar lists the next Monetary Policy Review and OCR decision for Wednesday, Oct. 28 at 2:00 p.m. NZT, with a media conference at 3:00 p.m. AlphaGen notes the MPC framed the move as gradual removal of stimulus, so fuel-driven inflation is the variable that frames that review.
items.source_name: Reserve Bank of New Zealand: Monetary Policy Review and OCR, October 2026

items.headline: Bank of Korea calendar: Q3 advance GDP Oct. 27; September interest rates Oct. 29
items.take: The Bank of Korea's statistical calendar lists the Q3 2026 real GDP advance estimate for Oct. 27 at 08:00 and the Consumer Survey Index for October the same day at 06:00. September interest-rate statistics follow on Oct. 29 at 12:00, and the preliminary September balance of payments on Nov. 5 at 08:00. The calendar notes the times are when media can publish and the schedule may change; AlphaGen flags the GDP print as the main Asian growth data point ahead of this week's central bank meetings.

items.headline: Euro-area M3 growth 3.5% in August, up from 3.4% in July: ECB
items.take: The ECB reported annual M3 growth of 3.5% in August 2026, up from 3.4% in July, while the narrower M1 aggregate grew 2.9%, down from 3.1%. The ECB's release calendar lists the September monetary developments for Oct. 27 at 10:00 CET. AlphaGen notes broad money growth and M1 moved in opposite directions in August.
items.source_name: ECB: Monetary developments in the euro area, August 2026 (Sept. 25, 2026)

items.headline: Euro-area adjusted loans to firms grow 4.2% in August, down from 4.4%: ECB
items.take: The ECB said adjusted loans to non-financial corporations grew 4.2% annually in August 2026, down from 4.4% in July, while adjusted loans to households grew 3.1%, unchanged from July. AlphaGen notes the corporate-lending slowdown came as the ECB's Governing Council prepares for its Oct. 28-29 meeting.
items.source_name: ECB: Monetary developments in the euro area, August 2026 (Sept. 25, 2026)

items.headline: BoJ calendar: Outlook Report Oct. 30, Summary of Opinions Nov. 10, minutes Dec. 23
items.take: The Bank of Japan's schedule lists its October Monetary Policy Meeting for Oct. 29-30, with the Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices released Oct. 30. The Summary of Opinions is due Nov. 10 and the minutes Dec. 23. AlphaGen notes the Nov. 10 summary is the first look at individual board views after the meeting.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan: Monetary Policy Meetings schedule

items.headline: Euro-area current account surplus €9B in August, down from €27B in July: ECB
items.take: The ECB reported a seasonally and working-day adjusted euro-area current account surplus of €9 billion in August 2026, a decrease of €18 billion from €27 billion in July. Over the 12 months to August the surplus was €250 billion, or 1.5% of euro-area GDP, versus €290 billion (1.8%) a year earlier. AlphaGen notes the 12-month surplus has narrowed by €40 billion over the year.
items.source_name: ECB press release: Euro area monthly balance of payments, August 2026 (Oct. 20, 2026; Banque de France copy)

items.headline: Euro-area 12-month goods surplus €290B vs €320B a year earlier: ECB
items.take: In the 12 months to August 2026 the euro-area goods surplus was €290 billion, down from €320 billion a year earlier, while the services surplus rose to €153 billion from €140 billion. The secondary income deficit widened to €207 billion from €179 billion. AlphaGen notes the services surplus gain offset only part of the goods decline.
items.source_name: ECB press release: Euro area monthly balance of payments, August 2026 (Oct. 20, 2026; Banque de France copy)

items.headline: Non-residents' net buying of euro-area debt securities €659B over 12 months: ECB
items.take: Non-residents' net purchases of euro-area debt securities were €659 billion in the 12 months to August 2026, up from €412 billion a year earlier, and their net purchases of euro-area equity were €446 billion, up from €419 billion. Euro-area residents' net direct investment in non-euro area assets rose to €424 billion from €211 billion. AlphaGen notes the debt-security inflow figure is the largest of the portfolio flows in the release.
items.source_name: ECB press release: Euro area monthly balance of payments, August 2026 (Oct. 20, 2026; Banque de France copy)

items.headline: Eurosystem open market operations net balance falls €7.1B to €1,927.5B: ECB
items.take: The ECB's weekly statement for Oct. 16, 2026 shows the net balance of open market operations and standing facilities fell by €7.1 billion to €1,927.5 billion, primarily due to the change in the level of the deposit facility. Base money rose by €3.8 billion to €3,923.5 billion. AlphaGen notes the two measures moved in opposite directions on the week.
items.source_name: ECB consolidated financial statement of the Eurosystem as at Oct. 16, 2026 (Banque de France copy)

items.headline: Eurosystem holds €1,642.7B in PSPP and €1,268.8B in PEPP as of Oct. 16: ECB
items.take: Eurosystem holdings of securities for monetary policy purposes as of Oct. 16, 2026 included €1,642.7 billion under the public sector purchase programme (weekly redemptions €3.4 billion) and €1,268.8 billion under the pandemic emergency purchase programme (€0.8 billion). Corporate sector purchase programme holdings were €212.0 billion, covered bond programme 3 €185.6 billion and asset-backed securities €1.7 billion; those rows sum to €3,310.8 billion by AlphaGen's calculation. The statement lists no new purchases in any programme.
items.source_name: ECB consolidated financial statement of the Eurosystem as at Oct. 16, 2026 (Banque de France copy)

items.headline: Halliburton Q3 revenue $5.7B, diluted EPS $0.50; adjusted EPS $0.60
items.take: Halliburton reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $5.7 billion, flat with the second quarter, and net income attributable to the company of $417 million, or $0.50 per diluted share. Adjusted net income was $501 million, or $0.60 per diluted share, versus $461 million, or $0.55, in Q2. AlphaGen notes the release compares against the prior quarter rather than the year-ago period.

items.headline: Halliburton: Completion and Production revenue $3.1B; ~$250M repurchased in Q3
items.take: Halliburton's Completion and Production revenue was $3.1 billion, down $113 million (4%) sequentially, with operating income of $457 million; Drilling and Evaluation revenue was $2.6 billion, up $102 million (4%), with operating income of $391 million. The company repurchased approximately $250 million of common stock and paid dividends of $0.17 per share in the quarter. AlphaGen reads the segment split as the two divisions moving in opposite directions from Q2.

items.headline: Hasbro Q3 revenue $1,595.3M, up 15%; diluted EPS $2.77 vs $1.64
items.take: Hasbro reported third-quarter 2026 net revenues of $1,595.3 million versus $1,387.5 million a year earlier, and net earnings attributable to Hasbro of $394.5 million versus $233.2 million. Diluted EPS was $2.77 versus $1.64; adjusted diluted EPS was $2.90 versus $1.68. AlphaGen notes Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming revenue of $747.2 million, up from $572.0 million, was the largest driver of the increase.

items.headline: Hasbro raises 2026 outlook: revenue growth 7-9% in constant currency
items.take: Hasbro's 2026 guidance calls for total revenue up 7% to 9% in constant currency, previously 5% to 7%, and adjusted operating margin of 27% to 28%, previously 25% to 26%. Adjusted EBITDA is guided to $1.575 billion to $1.625 billion, versus $1.45 billion to $1.50 billion before. AlphaGen notes all three measures moved up together in the release.

items.headline: CFTC: WTI crude managed money long 163,413, short 127,226 as of Oct. 20
items.take: CFTC's Oct. 20 report shows NYMEX WTI-Physical managed money long positions at 163,413 contracts (down 8,560 on the week) and short at 127,226 (down 4,173), a net long of 36,187 contracts. Open interest was 1,835,144, down 65,035 from Oct. 13. AlphaGen notes both sides of managed-money positioning shrank alongside the drop in open interest.
items.source_name: CFTC Commitments of Traders, Petroleum (Futures Only), Oct. 20, 2026

items.headline: CFTC: gold non-commercial longs 237,142 contracts; copper open interest up 13,287
items.take: CFTC's Oct. 20 futures-only report shows COMEX gold non-commercial long positions at 237,142 contracts (down 8,158) against shorts of 37,277 (down 144), with open interest of 402,279, up 5,934. Copper open interest rose 13,287 to 327,119, with non-commercial longs of 98,535 (down 9,024). AlphaGen notes this report groups traders as non-commercial rather than managed money.
items.source_name: CFTC Commitments of Traders, CMX (Futures Only), Oct. 20, 2026

items.headline: Treasury dealer agenda: dealer meetings set for Oct. 29-30; responses due Oct. 26
items.take: Treasury's November 2026 dealer agenda lists Treasury Dealer Meetings on Oct. 29 to Oct. 30, 2026, with a response deadline of 12:00 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 26. The document does not give dates for a refunding announcement, refunding statement or financing estimates. AlphaGen notes the dealer meetings fall in the same week as the FOMC and Q3 GDP releases.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury: Dealer Agenda, November 2026 (OMB Control No. 1505-0261)

items.headline: Fed H.10: broad dollar index at 121.4048 on Oct. 16; euro $1.1231, yen 158.00
items.take: The Fed's H.10 release dated Oct. 19 lists a broad dollar index of 121.4048 on Oct. 16, versus 122.0037 on Oct. 14 and 121.4433 on Oct. 13. The euro was $1.1231 per euro, the British pound $1.3330 per pound and the yen 158.00 per dollar on Oct. 16. The index was 0.5989 points below its Oct. 14 reading, and the Fed's next H.10 posting, Oct. 26 at 4:15 p.m. ET, will show how the dollar fared going into the FOMC week.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: H.10 Foreign Exchange Rates, Oct. 19, 2026

items.headline: 1-year Treasury yield 4.41% on Oct. 22, down 11 bp in a day; 6-month 4.29%
items.take: Fed H.15 shows the 1-year constant-maturity Treasury yield at 4.41% on Oct. 22, down from 4.52% on Oct. 21, and the 6-month yield at 4.29%, down from 4.35%. The 1-year sits 53 bp above the 3.88% effective federal funds rate. With the FOMC meeting Oct. 27-28, the gap between the 1-year yield and the funds rate is a figure worth watching.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: H.15 Selected Interest Rates, Oct. 22, 2026

items.headline: Fed H.15: bank prime loan rate 7.00%, 3.00 points above 4.00% primary credit rate
items.take: The H.15 release lists the bank prime loan rate at 7.00% and the discount window primary credit rate at 4.00% on both Oct. 21 and Oct. 22. The effective federal funds rate was 3.88% on each day. Prime-linked borrowing costs, such as many credit card and small-business loans, would move with the policy rate if the FOMC changes the target range on Oct. 28.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: H.15 Selected Interest Rates, Oct. 22, 2026

items.headline: Fed H.8: bank loans and leases $14,213.7B in week to Oct. 14, up $29.3B
items.take: Loans and leases in bank credit at all U.S. commercial banks stood at $14,213.7B in the week ended Oct. 14, up $29.3B from $14,184.4B a week earlier, seasonally adjusted. Total assets rose $38.0B to $26,138.3B. The next H.8 is scheduled for Oct. 30 at 4:15 p.m. ET and will show whether loan growth continued into the FOMC week.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: H.8 Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks, Oct. 23, 2026

items.headline: Fed H.8: bank Treasury and agency securities $4,783.8B, up $21.6B on the week
items.take: Commercial banks held $4,783.8B of Treasury and agency securities in the week ended Oct. 14, up $21.6B from $4,762.2B. Total securities in bank credit were $5,781.4B, up $16.3B, seasonally adjusted. Banks added to their government-backed holdings in the week, with cash assets little changed at $3,213.5B, up $5.2B.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: H.8 Assets and Liabilities of Commercial Banks, Oct. 23, 2026

items.headline: Fed calendar: no speeches or hearings listed Oct. 26-31; H.10 and CP data due Oct. 26
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's October calendar lists the two-day FOMC meeting on Oct. 27-28, with the press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET on Oct. 28, and no speeches, hearings or stress-test events for Oct. 26-31. Statistical releases include Commercial Paper at 1:00 p.m. and H.10 foreign exchange rates at 4:15 p.m. on Oct. 26, plus G.20 finance companies on Oct. 30 with an approximate publication date. The quiet speaker calendar leaves the FOMC statement and press conference as the main Fed communication of the week.

items.headline: Fed minutes: most participants saw another rate increase likely appropriate by year end
items.take: The minutes of the Sept. 15-16 FOMC meeting, last updated Oct. 7, say most participants judged that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end. The Committee had voted 12-0 to raise the range by 1/4 point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, and participants described inflation risk as skewed to the upside. With the next meeting on Oct. 27-28, the minutes frame the question as pace and timing of further tightening rather than whether it is on the table.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: FOMC minutes, Sept. 15-16, 2026

items.headline: Fed Sept. projections: median fed funds rate 4.1% for 2026, up from 3.8% in June
items.take: The Sept. 16 Summary of Economic Projections shows a median federal funds rate of 4.1% for 2026 (June: 3.8%), 4.1% for 2027 (3.6%) and 3.9% for 2028 (3.4%), with a longer-run median of 3.2% (3.1%). The current target range is 3-3/4 to 4 percent, so the 2026 median sits above the top of that range. The projections move the rate path higher in every year shown, which is the backdrop for the Oct. 27-28 meeting.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: FOMC projection materials, Sept. 16, 2026

items.headline: Fed Sept. projections: 2026 PCE inflation 3.7%, core 3.4%, unemployment 4.1%, GDP 2.3%
items.take: Median FOMC projections from Sept. 16 for 2026 are: PCE inflation 3.7% (June: 3.6%), core PCE inflation 3.4% (3.3%), unemployment rate 4.1% (4.3%) and real GDP growth 2.3% (2.2%). For 2027, PCE inflation is projected at 2.3% and core at 2.5%, unchanged from June. Officials marked inflation up and unemployment down for 2026, a combination that supports the case for firmer policy.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: FOMC projection materials, Sept. 16, 2026

items.headline: BLS: PPI final demand up 6.3% in 12 months to September, largest since December 2022
items.take: The Producer Price Index for final demand rose 6.3% over the 12 months ended September 2026, which BLS describes as the largest 12-month increase since 6.4% in December 2022. Final demand goods rose 9.8% and final demand services 4.9%; the data are not seasonally adjusted and subject to revision for four months. The goods-services gap shows how much of the pipeline pressure is concentrated in physical inputs.
items.source_name: BLS: The Economics Daily, Producer Price Index up 6.3 percent in September

items.headline: BLS PPI: gasoline up 64.3%, No. 2 diesel up 115.2% over 12 months to September
items.take: BLS reports final demand energy prices up 35.4% over the 12 months ended September, led by gasoline (+64.3%), No. 2 diesel (+115.2%) and home heating oil and distillates (+117.5%). Transportation and warehousing services rose 16.0%, including truck freight and water freight (both +19.3%) and airline passenger services (+16.6%). Fuel costs appear to be passing into freight and travel prices, which is how an energy shock reaches services.
items.source_name: BLS: The Economics Daily, Producer Price Index up 6.3 percent in September

items.headline: Fed minutes: interest on reserve balances raised to 3.90%, primary credit rate to 4.0%
items.take: The Sept. 15-16 FOMC minutes record that the interest rate on reserve balances was raised to 3.90 percent and the primary credit rate to 4.0 percent alongside the 1/4-point increase in the target range to 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The minutes also say the Desk had paused reserve management purchases and that the pace of future purchases was not on a preset course. Both rates are administered by the Fed, so they will move only if the Committee changes policy on Oct. 28.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board: FOMC minutes, Sept. 15-16, 2026

items.headline: Fed calendar: FOMC meets Oct. 27-28; press conference Oct. 28 at 2:30 p.m. ET
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's calendar lists a two-day FOMC meeting on Oct. 27-28, with the press conference on Oct. 28 at 2:30 p.m. ET. The calendar does not list a separate statement time. The meeting is the main scheduled U.S. policy event of the week, and it lands one day before the first estimate of third-quarter GDP.

items.headline: BEA schedules third-quarter GDP advance estimate and September income for Oct. 29
items.take: BEA's release schedule lists the advance estimate of third-quarter 2026 GDP and the September Personal Income and Outlays report for Oct. 29 at 8:30. Both arrive the day after the FOMC press conference, so the Fed's comments will come before the first read on the quarter. BEA also lists September international trade for Nov. 4.

items.headline: BLS Employment Cost Index for Q3 due Oct. 30 at 8:30 a.m. ET
items.take: BLS lists the Employment Cost Index for the third quarter of 2026 for Friday, Oct. 30 at 8:30 a.m. ET. It is the only BLS release on the schedule for the final day of the week. The ECI measures employer labor costs, which makes it one of the labor-cost gauges that sits alongside the BEA's income data the day before.

items.headline: ECB Governing Council holds monetary policy meeting Oct. 28-29; press conference Oct. 29
items.take: The ECB's calendar lists the monetary policy meeting in Frankfurt on Oct. 28 and 29, with the press conference following on Oct. 29. The next meeting after that is Dec. 16-17, and the calendar does not list press conference times. The Oct. 29 decision day also coincides with BEA's third-quarter GDP release.

items.headline: BLS: no releases Oct. 26-27; metro-area jobs and business dynamics data Oct. 28
items.take: BLS lists no releases for Oct. 26 or 27. On Wednesday, Oct. 28 at 10:00 a.m. ET it schedules Metropolitan Area Employment and Unemployment for September and Business Employment Dynamics for the first quarter of 2026. Consumer Expenditures for annual 2025 follows on Oct. 29 at 10:00 a.m. ET, so the early-week labor-data calendar is thin.

items.headline: Fed statistical calendar: H.6 money stock Oct. 27; H.4.1 balance sheet Oct. 29
items.take: The Federal Reserve Board's calendar lists H.6 (Money Stock Measures) on Oct. 27 at 1:00 p.m. and the H.4.1 balance sheet report on Oct. 29 at 4:30 p.m. H.8 bank assets and liabilities follows on Oct. 30 at 4:15 p.m., with H.15 rates published each day at 4:15 p.m. The H.4.1 will be the first weekly balance sheet look after the policy meeting.

items.headline: Treasury par curve: 10-year at 5.00% and 30-year at 5.33% on Oct. 23
items.take: Treasury's daily par yield curve for Oct. 23 showed the 2-year at 4.69%, 10-year at 5.00% and 30-year at 5.33%, each 4 basis points above Oct. 22. The 10-year was 15 basis points below its 5.15% on Oct. 19, and the 3-month bill at 4.22% sat 78 basis points under the 10-year.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury Daily Par Yield Curve Rates

items.headline: Treasury curve: 20-year yield 5.37% sits above 30-year at 5.33% on Oct. 23
items.take: Treasury's par yield curve showed the 20-year at 5.37% and the 30-year at 5.33% on Oct. 23, a 4 basis point inversion between the two longest maturities. The 7-year was 4.89% and the 10-year 5.00%, so the curve rises to the 20-year point and then dips slightly. The 20-year was 5.32% on Oct. 22.
items.source_name: U.S. Treasury Daily Par Yield Curve Rates

items.headline: 10-year breakeven inflation rate at 2.34% on Oct. 23, up from 2.32%
items.take: The 10-year breakeven inflation rate, derived from nominal and inflation-indexed Treasury yields, was 2.34% on Oct. 23, 2026. It was 2.32% on Oct. 22, 2.37% on Oct. 21, and 2.35% on both Oct. 20 and Oct. 19. The range across the five observations is five basis points, suggesting market-implied inflation expectations were steady even as nominal yields moved.

items.headline: 10-year TIPS real yield falls to 2.64% on Oct. 22 from 2.76% a day earlier
items.take: The 10-year inflation-indexed Treasury yield was 2.64% on Oct. 22, 2026, down 12 basis points from 2.76% on Oct. 21 and 16 basis points below 2.80% on Oct. 19. Nominal 10-year yields fell 17 basis points over the same two days (5.13% to 4.96%), so most of the decline came from real yields rather than breakevens.

items.headline: Fed overnight reverse repo take-up $0.2B on Oct. 23, little changed from earlier in week
items.take: Treasury securities sold in the Fed's overnight reverse repurchase operations totaled $0.200 billion on Oct. 23, 2026, versus $0.351 billion on Oct. 22, $0.237 billion on Oct. 21, $0.227 billion on Oct. 20 and $0.330 billion on Oct. 19. Usage has stayed under $0.4 billion all week, indicating minimal use of the facility.

items.headline: BioNTech, BMS report Phase 2 pumitamig data in second-line NSCLC at ESMO
items.take: In the single-arm Phase 2 ROSETTA Lung-107 study (abstract LBA76 at ESMO 2026), pumitamig 1400 mg plus docetaxel showed a confirmed objective response rate of 36.7% and disease control rate of 90.0% in 30 efficacy-evaluable patients. Median progression-free survival in 50 treated patients was 6.9 months; grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 18.0%. BMS said it looks forward to defining the path forward for pumitamig in second-line NSCLC; overall survival was not reported.
items.source_name: BioNTech and Bristol Myers Squibb release (GlobeNewswire, Oct. 25, 2026)

items.headline: Genmab reports petosemtamab Phase 2 colorectal data: ORR 75% first-line, 67% second-line
items.take: Genmab presented updated Phase 2 data at ESMO 2026 for petosemtamab plus FOLFOX or FOLFIRI in 79 treated patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (45 first-line, 34 second-line). Objective response rates (confirmed and unconfirmed) were 75% first-line and 67% second-line, with disease control rates of 95% and 93%. Median follow-up was 5.9 and 7.1 months, and Genmab will hold an investor update Oct. 28 at 12:00 p.m. EDT.

items.headline: Chicago Fed NFCI at -0.496 for week ended Oct. 16, looser than average
items.take: The Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index read -0.496 for the week ending October 16, 2026, up from -0.502 the prior week and -0.508 on October 2. Per the series notes, positive values indicate financial conditions tighter than average, so a negative reading means looser than average. Conditions have stayed loose while edging up for three straight weeks; the next reading is due October 28.

items.headline: Chicago Fed adjusted NFCI at -0.518 for week ended Oct. 16
items.take: The Chicago Fed's Adjusted National Financial Conditions Index, which isolates financial conditions uncorrelated with economic conditions, was -0.518 for the week ending October 16, 2026, versus -0.524 the prior week. Negative values indicate conditions looser than average. Both the adjusted and unadjusted gauges rose by 0.006 on the week, computed from the published readings.

items.headline: Fed note: semiliquid retail funds grew from $15B in 2018 to $388B in 2025
items.take: A Federal Reserve Board FEDS Note by Logan George and Chaehee Shin finds total net assets of interval funds, tender offer funds and non-traded perpetual-life BDCs rose from $15 billion in 2018 to $388 billion in 2025, while total mutual fund net assets grew 33% over the same period. The interval and tender offer figures are lower-bound estimates, and non-traded BDC assets were about $307 billion at 2025Q4. The growth rate of roughly 26 times in seven years makes these vehicles a fast-growing channel for retail exposure to private credit.

items.headline: Fed note: interval funds hold 49.5% private credit; non-traded BDC debt-to-equity 0.90
items.take: In the Fed Board's 2025Q4 sample of 207 funds, interval funds held 49.5% of value-weighted assets in private credit, tender offer funds 13.4%, and non-traded BDCs 93.4% in loans. Average debt-to-equity was 0.27 for interval funds, 0.09 for tender offer funds and 0.90 for non-traded BDCs, and average default or non-accrual rates were 0.6%, 2.4% and 1.4%. The note cites defined contribution plans holding over $13.9 trillion as of September 2025, which frames why retail access to these funds draws regulatory attention.

items.headline: CFTC: 10-year note futures show asset managers net long 2.93M, leveraged funds net short 2.11M
items.take: CFTC's Traders in Financial Futures report for October 20, 2026 shows UST 10Y note open interest of 5,868,295 contracts, with asset managers long 3,675,600 and short 750,184 (net long 2,925,416) and leveraged funds long 567,553 and short 2,674,777 (net short 2,107,224). Those net figures are computed from the report's long and short columns. Asset managers and leveraged funds sit on opposite sides of the 10-year contract, with asset managers' net long equal to about 50% of open interest.
items.source_name: CFTC, Traders in Financial Futures (Oct. 20 data)

items.headline: CFTC: 2-year note futures asset managers net long 1.72M vs leveraged funds net short 1.29M
items.take: In CFTC's October 20, 2026 financial futures report, UST 2Y note open interest was 4,533,571 contracts: asset managers were long 2,461,884 and short 738,304 (net long 1,723,580), while leveraged funds were long 771,136 and short 2,056,684 (net short 1,285,548). items.source_name: CFTC, Traders in Financial Futures (Oct. 20 data)

items.headline: NY Fed: each 1-pt rise in average tariffs lifts consumer goods prices about 0.25%
items.take: New York Fed staff (Amiti, Heise, Weinstein) estimate that each one-percentage-point rise in average tariffs raises consumer goods prices by about 0.25% after one year, with roughly two-thirds coming through imported consumer goods. They find about 90% of the 2025 tariffs passed through to U.S. import prices, and project the tariff contribution to 12-month inflation reaching roughly zero by August 2026 before turning negative. The authors' result frames tariffs as a price-level effect that drops out of year-over-year comparisons, which matters for how goods inflation is read.
items.source_name: New York Fed, Liberty Street Economics (Oct. 6)

items.headline: NY Fed study: most firms' investment responds little to monetary policy
items.take: A New York Fed Liberty Street post (Oct. 7) finds investment by most firms in most periods responds little to monetary policy, though investment falls when rates rise for all firms. For about 5% of firm-quarters, a monetary shock raising the fed funds rate 1 percentage point lowers capital growth by 4 percentage points, and small and young firms respond most. The takeaway is that rate transmission runs through a minority of firms at any given time, with the sample limited to publicly listed Compustat firms.
items.source_name: New York Fed, Liberty Street Economics (Oct. 7)

items.headline: BOJ's Koeda: neutral rate 'considerably above 1 percent' ahead of Oct. 29-30 meeting
items.take: In an Oct. 15 speech, BOJ Policy Board member Junko Koeda said the September hike raised the overnight call rate to around 1.25%, that the neutral interest rate is "considerably above 1 percent," and that the Bank "should not become overly cautious about raising the policy interest rate." She also said the median of item-level inflation is in the early 2% range. Her remarks are one board member's view and set the tone going into the Oct. 29-30 meeting, which carries an Outlook Report.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan (speech by Junko Koeda, Oct. 15)

items.headline: BOJ Sept. meeting opinions: several backed a hike, others favored holding
items.take: The BOJ's Summary of Opinions for the Sept. 17-18 meeting, released Oct. 1, shows several members supported raising the policy rate while others preferred holding because CPI had been below 2%. Members described underlying inflation as "fairly close to 2 percent" and said further hikes should be gradual and flexible, with the pace faster if upward price deviation appears. The split on timing is the backdrop for the Oct. 29-30 meeting.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan, Summary of Opinions (Sept. 17-18 meeting)

items.headline: Treasury tentative schedule: 2-, 5-, 7-year notes and 2-year FRN auction Oct. 26-29
items.take: Treasury's tentative auction schedule lists a 2-year note on Oct. 26, a 5-year note on Oct. 27, a 2-year FRN on Oct. 28 and a 7-year note on Oct. 29, all settling Nov. 2. items.headline: Bank of Canada to announce rate decision Oct. 28 at 9:45 a.m. ET with Monetary Policy Report
items.take: The Bank of Canada will announce its overnight rate target decision on Oct. 28 at 9:45 a.m. ET, together with the Monetary Policy Report; Governor Macklem and Senior Deputy Governor Rogers hold a press conference at about 10:30 a.m. ET. The Bank's Sept. 2 release set the overnight rate target at 2.25%, with a Bank Rate of 2.5% and deposit rate of 2.20%. The decision lands the same day as the FOMC statement.

items.headline: Bank of Japan meets Oct. 29-30; Outlook Report due Oct. 30

The BOJ meeting closes out a run of major central bank decisions that includes the FOMC and ECB earlier in the same week.
items.source_name: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meetings

items.headline: Eurostat calendar lists euro-area Q3 preliminary GDP flash for Oct. 30
items.take: Eurostat's quarterly national accounts calendar lists the preliminary Q3 2026 GDP flash release for Friday, Oct. 30, with the fuller employment and GDP flash on Nov. 13. items.headline: Fed G.17: September industrial production up 0.7%, 2.2% above a year earlier
items.take: The Federal Reserve's G.17 release says industrial production rose 0.7 percent in September after edging up 0.1 percent in August, with August revised up from 0.0 percent. Total output stood at 104.0 percent of its 2017 average and was 2.2 percent above its year-earlier level. Utilities output rose 3.5 percent in the month, so the headline gain leaned on weather-sensitive output more than on factories.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board G.17 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Fed G.17: capacity utilization 76.9% in September; manufacturing output up 0.3%
items.take: Capacity utilization moved up to 76.9 percent in September, the Fed reported, with August revised up from 76.3 percent to 76.4 percent. Manufacturing output rose 0.3 percent in September, and August was revised from -0.3 percent to -0.2 percent. Mining output rose 0.2 percent; the factory gain was far smaller than the 0.7 percent increase in the overall index.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board G.17 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Fed adds private credit to Financial Accounts from September 2026 release
items.take: A Fed Board FEDS Note dated Oct. 16 says private credit assets under management reached over $2.6 trillion as of 2025:Q4, up from about $350 billion in 2012, and that integration into the Financial Accounts (Z.1) begins with the September 2026 release. Private credit was about 6 percent of total nonfinancial business debt in 2025:Q4 ($1.31 trillion of $23.29 trillion). The authors say the change does not substantially change business-debt trends overall, but it gives policymakers a first official sector-level view of a market that was previously recorded mostly as miscellaneous liabilities.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Note: Introducing Private Credit into the Financial Accounts of the United States (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Fed note sizes private credit: private debt funds $939B, BDCs $572B in assets
items.take: The Fed's FEDS Note puts 2025:Q4 assets at about $939 billion for private debt funds, with private credit loans about 60 percent of that, and about $572 billion for business development companies, about 80 percent in private credit loans. Interval and tender offer funds held about $292 billion, up from $100 billion in 2021, and middle-market CLOs held $54 billion of private credit loans. The fast growth of the interval-fund channel is the part of the estimate worth watching.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Note: Introducing Private Credit into the Financial Accounts of the United States (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.headline: Fed note: stock-bond correlation turned negative after 2021, weakening bond hedge
items.take: A Fed FEDS Note (Oct. 16) finds the correlation of U.S. stock returns with changes in 10-year yields was 0.4 in 2000-2021 and -0.09 after 2021; the euro-area figures were 0.41 and -0.02 and the U.K.'s 0.31 and -0.14. The U.S. 10-year yield's response to inflation news rose from a coefficient of 0.048 (2000-2019) to 0.155 post-2021. The authors attribute the shift to inflation dynamics and the mix of shocks, not to a change in bonds themselves, and say the hedge could improve if inflation eases.
items.source_name: Federal Reserve Board FEDS Note: Government Bonds' Safe-Haven Property and Inflationary Pressures (Oct. 16, 2026)

items.take: Midland States Bancorp reported Q3 2026 net income available to common shareholders of $20.6 million ($22.8 million before preferred dividends) and diluted EPS of $0.95, versus $0.24 in Q3 2025. items.headline: First American Q3 net income $177.0M, diluted EPS $1.72 vs $1.84 a year earlier

items.headline: Columbia Banking Q3 diluted EPS $0.78 vs $0.40; net interest margin 4.11%
